Key Highlights:
Over the 2023–2024 period, chocolate retail operations generated $1.28M in total revenue and $510.5K in profit across 50,000 transactions. The average profit margin stands at 40.0%, with an average order value of $25.51.

Year-over-year, revenue moved +1.7% from 2023 to 2024, while profit shifted +1.6%. Order volume changed by +1.5%. Discount utilization across all transactions is 37.5%, with 18,774 orders receiving some form of discount.

Seasonally, Jul was the strongest revenue month (combined across both years), while Feb was the weakest.

Trend Insights:
The monthly revenue trend shows relatively stable performance across the two-year period. Jul consistently ranks as the peak month for revenue, suggesting seasonality — potentially linked to holiday gifting seasons. Feb represents the trough, which could be an opportunity for targeted promotional campaigns. The quarterly view reveals whether growth is accelerating or decelerating across the business cycle.

Discount Insights:
The data reveals a clear relationship between discount depth and margin compression. Full-price (no discount) transactions achieve an average margin of 40.0%, while discounted transactions average 40.0%.

However, discounted orders show similar average quantities per order (2.99 vs 3.00 units), suggesting discounts may not significantly drive volume uplift. The margin-vs-volume chart above shows whether this volume gain compensates for the margin erosion at each discount tier.

Recommendation: Management should evaluate whether deep discounts (>15%) are generating enough incremental volume and customer acquisition to justify the margin sacrifice. A tiered approach — limiting deep discounts to specific products or customer segments — may optimize the trade-off.

Customer Insights:
The customer base of 31,531 unique buyers shows a repeat purchase rate of 42.0%. The spending tier analysis reveals classic Pareto dynamics — Platinum-tier customers (top 25%) contribute 50.4% of total revenue.

Platinum customers average 2.4 orders versus 1.1 for Bronze-tier. This gap suggests that retention and engagement programs targeting mid-tier customers could meaningfully increase their order frequency and lifetime value.
